## Boltz-2

Predict unified three-dimensional structures for complexes containing proteins, DNA, RNA, and/or small-molecule ligands, with confidence and affinity outputs when applicable.

### Public interface guidance

Predict biomolecular structures for supported combinations of proteins, nucleic acids and ligands using Boltz2. Supply the entity sequences or ligand SMILES to compare. Predictions are scheduled as pairs, including first-versus-rest comparisons within a polymer type and supported combinations across entity types.

This table describes the product interface. The connector's exact request schema, file checks, input limits and execution notices below remain authoritative. Product labels are not automatic API aliases or permission to use unsupported values; do not infer unverified field mappings.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_name` | string | Required | envelope | Tool identifier: Boltz2. It selects the tool, not the experiment label. The connector generates experiment_name when omitted; preserve an exact label only when supplied by the user. |
| `Protein_Sequences` | array | Optional | value | Protein amino-acid sequences to model. Keep each protein as a separate entity. An unused entity type may be left empty; the complete request must contain at least one usable protein or nucleic-acid sequence. For API requests, send a JSON array of strings. Use [] when this entity type is unused; do not send an empty string or a list containing an empty string. |
| `DNA_Sequences` | array | Optional | value | DNA nucleotide sequences to model, with each sequence supplied as a separate entity. Leave empty when the prediction does not include DNA. For API requests, send a JSON array of strings. Use [] when this entity type is unused; do not send an empty string or a list containing an empty string. |
| `RNA_Sequences` | array | Optional | value | RNA nucleotide sequences to model, with each sequence supplied as a separate entity. Leave empty when the prediction does not include RNA. For API requests, send a JSON array of strings. Use [] when this entity type is unused; do not send an empty string or a list containing an empty string. |
| `SMILES` | array | Optional | value | Ligand structures expressed as SMILES, with one complete SMILES string per entity. Preserve each string as a unit; punctuation within a SMILES string is part of the molecular representation. Leave empty when no ligand is needed. For API requests, send a JSON array of strings. Use [] when this entity type is unused; do not send an empty string or a list containing an empty string. |

An experiment label is generated by the connector when omitted. Keep an exact label only when the user supplied one; use the submission envelope below.

Product result guidance: Prediction bundles, a ZIP of structures and a table of result paths. Inspect the confidence and affinity-related outputs where present. Supplying several entities does not request one arbitrary complex containing all of them.

A submission acknowledgement confirms receipt; wait for completion and inspect actual artifacts before interpreting or reporting results.

Exact job name: `Boltz2`.

## Monomer Structure Prediction

Monomer Structure Prediction

### Public interface guidance

Predict individual protein structures from amino-acid sequences using AlphaFold. Supply a CSV containing sequence identifiers and protein sequences. Each input sequence is treated as a monomer prediction.

This table describes the product interface. The connector's exact request schema, file checks, input limits and execution notices below remain authoritative. Product labels are not automatic API aliases or permission to use unsupported values; do not infer unverified field mappings.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_name` | string | Required | envelope | Tool identifier: Protein_Structure_Prediction. It selects the tool, not the experiment label. The connector generates experiment_name when omitted; preserve an exact label only when supplied by the user. |
| `experiment_name` | string | Required | envelope | Name you choose for this experiment. Use a meaningful label to identify the run and its results. |
| `input_csv` | string | Required | file | CSV containing sequences and exactly one identifier column named seq_id or sequence_id. Identifiers must be unique. Each row supplies one protein sequence; header matching is case-insensitive. Invalid rows may be excluded from results. |

An experiment label is generated by the connector when omitted. Keep an exact label only when the user supplied one; use the submission envelope below.

Product result guidance: A prediction table with confidence metrics and a ZIP of predicted structures. Check output coverage and confidence when interpreting individual predictions.

A submission acknowledgement confirms receipt; wait for completion and inspect actual artifacts before interpreting or reporting results.

Exact job name: `Protein_Structure_Prediction`.

Fields below belong in `experiment_data`. The connector generates `experiment_name` unless the user supplies one.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `input_csv` | string | yes | file | The identifier column may be sequence_id or seq_id; sequences is required. |
| `property_name` | string | no / mode-dependent | value | Default: `"monomer_structure_prediction"` |

Input kinds: `value` is inline data; `file` requires a platform file reference;

## Multimer Structure Prediction

Predict multimeric protein structures from paired or grouped sequences.

### Public interface guidance

Predict protein complex structures from grouped amino-acid sequences using AlphaFold-Multimer/ColabFold. Provide the component sequences in the desired chain order to model their assembly.

This table describes the product interface. The connector's exact request schema, file checks, input limits and execution notices below remain authoritative. Product labels are not automatic API aliases or permission to use unsupported values; do not infer unverified field mappings.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_name` | string | Required | envelope | Tool identifier: Multimer_Structure_Prediction. It selects the tool, not the experiment label. The connector generates experiment_name when omitted; preserve an exact label only when supplied by the user. |
| `input_path` | string | Required | value | Two or more protein amino-acid sequences joined by colons in one text value, in the desired chain order. Supply sequence text without a prefixed record identifier. This interface uses the sequence-text input mode. |

An experiment label is generated by the connector when omitted. Keep an exact label only when the user supplied one; use the submission envelope below.

Product result guidance: Predicted complex structures and confidence tables, including pLDDT and ipTM where available. Confidence measures describe the prediction and do not establish experimental binding.

A submission acknowledgement confirms receipt; wait for completion and inspect actual artifacts before interpreting or reporting results.

Exact job name: `Multimer_Structure_Prediction`.

### Inputs

Fields below belong in `experiment_data`. The connector generates `experiment_name` unless the user supplies one.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `input_path` | string | yes | value | Colon-separated input sequences as one string; the form sends this text unchanged in input_path. |

Input kinds: `value` is inline data; `file` requires a platform file reference;
`file_or_value` supports either documented mode; `artifact` is an authorized upstream result reference.
Only local files require a new upload. Never infer input mode from a field name.

## ipSAE Generation

Score protein-protein interfaces across AlphaFold2-multimer or Boltz2 prediction bundles using PAE, residue confidence, and inter-chain distance information.

### Public interface guidance

Calculate protein-interface confidence scores with ipSAE from AlphaFold2-Multimer or Boltz2 predictions. The analysis combines predicted structures with matched confidence and predicted aligned error information. Optional cutoffs control which residue pairs contribute to scoring.

This table describes the product interface. The connector's exact request schema, file checks, input limits and execution notices below remain authoritative. Product labels are not automatic API aliases or permission to use unsupported values; do not infer unverified field mappings.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `model_type` | string | Required | value | Prediction source: af2_multimer or boltz2. Select the type that matches the files in the uploaded archive. |
| `input_path` | string | Required | file | ZIP containing matched structures and confidence files. AF2-Multimer inputs need ranked PDBs and score JSON or JSON.GZ files. Boltz2 inputs need PDB/CIF structures and matching PAE NPZ files. A structure alone is insufficient. |
| `pae_cutoff` | number | Optional | value | Positive predicted aligned error cutoff, in angstroms. Fractional values are allowed. Omission uses 10.0; do not supply null. |
| `dist_cutoff` | number | Optional | value | Positive C-alpha distance cutoff, in angstroms. A smaller value selects closer residue pairs. Fractional values are allowed; omission uses 10.0. Do not supply null. |

An experiment label is generated by the connector when omitted. Keep an exact label only when the user supplied one; use the submission envelope below.

Product-interface limits (not overrides of connector validation): PAE and distance cutoffs must be positive numbers. Fractional values are accepted; each omitted cutoff defaults to 10.0 angstroms.

Product result guidance: A flattened CSV of interface scores. These scores describe confidence in a predicted interface and are not experimental affinity measurements.

A submission acknowledgement confirms receipt; wait for completion and inspect actual artifacts before interpreting or reporting results.

Exact job name: `ipsae-protein`.

### Inputs

Fields below belong in `experiment_data`. The connector generates `experiment_name` unless the user supplies one.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `model_type` | string | yes | value | Exact value `af2_multimer` or `boltz2`; choose it to match the archive producer. |
| `input_path` | string | yes | file | Uploaded ZIP containing compatible prediction structures and their matching confidence/PAE files. A lone PDB is insufficient. |
| `pae_cutoff` | number | no / mode-dependent | value | PAE threshold; worker default 10.0. |
| `dist_cutoff` | number | no / mode-dependent | value | C-alpha contact-distance threshold; worker default 10.0. |

Input kinds: `value` is inline data; `file` requires a platform file reference;
`file_or_value` supports either documented mode; `artifact` is an authorized upstream result reference.
Only local files require a new upload. Never infer input mode from a field name.
